ledger.x: 1692: Emperor Leopold I elevates Duke Ernest Augustus of Calenberg to elector, creating the Electorate of Hanover.
1715: Hanover takes Bremen-Verden from the Danes.
1719: the Treaty of Stockholm gives Hanover Bremen-Verden.
1757: the French invade Hanover and win at Hastenbeck.
1757: the Convention of Klosterzeven halts the fighting.
1802: Cliopatria's electorate row ends and its 'Kingdom of Hanover' row (1803-1865) takes the same realm.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Denmark-Norway occupied Bremen-Verden in 1712 and sold it to George I in 1715; Hanover took de facto possession and Sweden ceded it in the 1719 Treaty of Stockholm for 1 million rixdollars.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: The French defeated the Anglo-Hanoverian army at Hastenbeck (26 July 1757) and occupied Hanover after the Convention of Klosterzeven (September 1757); the convention was disavowed and the French expelled in 1758; at Minden (1 August 1759) 'the battle ended…

wars.name: Prussian occupation of Hanover (1801)
wars.outcome: 24,000 Prussian soldiers occupied the electorate without a fight and stayed until October 1801; no change of ownership.

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundary lines; the electorate was a patchwork (the page lists Calenberg, Grubenhagen, Lüneburg, Diepholz, Hoya, Saxe-Lauenburg, Bremen-Verden, Hadeln) drawn as Cliopatria's generalised shape.
